strengths: The feed-forward, unposed 3D stylization setting is practically important, and separating geometry prediction from style-conditioned Gaussian colors is an intuitive design.
The paper is generally clear and includes useful ablations of attention variants, style-loss variants, view count, runtime, and memory.
Qualitative results across CO3D, DL3DV-10K, and Tanks and Temples show appealing stylization, reasonable structural preservation, and promising cross-scene/category generalization.
Inference is substantially more convenient than per-scene optimization approaches, and the reported consistency results outperform StyleRF and StyleGS on the four evaluated scenes.
weaknesses: The central global-versus-frame attention distinction is technically unclear. Under Eqs. 1–2, each query attends independently to the same style keys and values, so concatenating queries from all views does not itself create cross-view coupling. The paper does not explain what operation makes global attention mathematically different, undermining a key claimed contribution and its ablation.

The proposed 3D loss is internally inconsistent. Equation 6 and the main text describe statistics over jointly fused multi-view voxels, but Algorithm 3 voxelizes each view separately and immediately computes its statistics, with no visible cross-view accumulation. This ambiguity directly affects the method's central novelty and reproducibility.

The evaluation does not adequately measure reference-style fidelity. ArtScore is reference-free and measures generic artness, while raw LPIPS/RMSE between different camera frames primarily reflects image/viewpoint changes rather than correspondence-aware 3D consistency. No user study, style-similarity metric, or flow/correspondence-based temporal evaluation is provided.

State-of-the-art comparison is narrow: only two older baselines and four Tanks and Temples scenes are evaluated, with no quantitative comparison to the closely related feed-forward Styl3R. It is also insufficiently explained whether released per-scene baseline models, rendering conditions, styles, and preprocessing make the comparison fair.

Claims of geometry preservation and broad generalization are weakly supported. Reconstruction metrics appear only in a three-category attention ablation, rather than comparisons against reconstruction backbones or stylization baselines, and the held-out-category evaluation lacks complete aggregate quantitative results.
The claim of scaling to hundreds of views is not demonstrated. Experiments reach only 64 views, quality reportedly deteriorates beyond 32, and training uses at most 24 views.

Important implementation details are missing, including loss weights, voxel resolution and bounds, architectural dimensions, dataset sampling/splits, optimization schedule, training cost, rendering resolution, and baseline configuration. The code link is empty and release is conditional on acceptance, so the current submission is not reproducible.

The method's novelty is moderate because it largely combines pretrained VGGT/AnySplat machinery with standard cross-attention and AdaIN-style statistics; given the ambiguities and limited evaluation, the evidence does not yet establish a sufficiently strong advance for a top-tier venue.

strengths: The paper targets a useful problem: feed-forward stylization of unposed multi-view inputs without scene-specific optimization.

Separating geometry prediction from style-conditioned color prediction is intuitive and potentially practical, and the method scales to substantially more views than several prior feed-forward approaches.
The manuscript is generally understandable and includes useful qualitative examples, architectural ablations, and basic runtime and memory measurements.
Some reported results favor Stylos over StyleRF and StyleGS, while the visual examples suggest reasonable geometry preservation in several cases.
weaknesses: The central 3D-style-loss contribution is internally inconsistent. Equation 6 describes statistics over features fused across views into a scene-level voxel grid, but Algorithm 3 voxelizes and computes statistics separately inside the loop over views. As written, the implementation does not perform the claimed multi-view fusion and therefore does not directly enforce the advertised cross-view constraint.

The consistency evaluation is insufficiently defined and potentially invalid. The paper reports LPIPS and RMSE between different camera frames without describing geometric or optical-flow warping, visibility masks, or correspondence handling. Direct differences between frames largely measure viewpoint and scene-content changes, and can favor blurry outputs rather than genuinely consistent 3D stylization.

The evaluation does not convincingly measure style-transfer fidelity. ArtScore is reference-free and measures generic artness rather than similarity to the supplied style. There is no human study or reference-conditioned perceptual/style metric, so high ArtScore cannot substantiate faithful transfer of arbitrary styles.

The cross-attention ablation uses the first content frame as the style reference and evaluates PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS against reconstruction targets. It therefore tests reconstruction under near-identity conditioning, not the claimed ability of global cross-attention to improve arbitrary stylization or style consistency.

The proposed 3D loss yields only very small numerical gains over the image and scene losses, with no variance, confidence intervals, repeated-run analysis, or statistical testing. Its qualitative comparison is limited to a few selected examples.

The state-of-the-art comparison is narrow and potentially confounded: it includes only two older per-scene methods, omits the most directly related feed-forward method Styl3R, and compares released per-scene weights against a newly trained general model without establishing matched training data, style references, rendering settings, or computational budgets.

Major claims are overstated. The paper claims operation on hundreds of views, yet experiments show at most 64 views and explicitly report degradation beyond 32; training uses no more than 24 views. Zero-shot generalization is demonstrated on only three held-out CO3D categories and four Tanks and Temples scenes.

Important technical details are missing, including voxel bounds and resolution, occupied-voxel masking and normalization, feature fusion rules, loss weights, training schedules, data sampling, exact splits, rendering resolution, and architecture dimensions. Empty accumulation and ambiguous reduction logic in the loss pseudocode further undermine reproducibility, while code is only promised after acceptance.

There is no quantitative evaluation of geometry, camera estimation, or novel-view reconstruction under genuine style conditioning, despite geometry preservation and unposed-input reconstruction being central claims.

The qualitative results reveal substantial smoothing, weak style transfer in some examples, and occasional structural or view-dependent artifacts. The paper provides no failure-case analysis, user evaluation, or systematic assessment of these limitations.

strengths: The paper tackles an important practical problem and proposes an appealing capability: feed-forward 3D stylization from unposed inputs without per-scene optimization.

The separation of self-attention-based geometry prediction from globally style-conditioned color prediction is intuitive, clearly motivated, and compatible with modern feed-forward Gaussian-splatting pipelines.
The voxel-space style objective is a potentially useful contribution for incorporating 3D structure into otherwise image-level feature-statistics matching.
The ablations support global cross-attention over frame-only and hybrid alternatives, and the 3D loss gives modest but consistent improvements in the reported long-range consistency metrics.
Stylos outperforms the evaluated StyleRF and StyleGS baselines on most consistency and ArtScore measurements while avoiding their per-scene optimization requirements.
The qualitative results are extensive and generally show attractive stylization, recognizable scene structure, and reasonable consistency across viewpoints.
The method has favorable practical scaling: reported inference time and memory grow approximately linearly with the number of input views.
weaknesses: The evaluation does not convincingly measure style fidelity. ArtScore is reference-free and measures general artistic appearance rather than agreement with the supplied style image, while no style-similarity metric, preference study, or human evaluation is provided.

The cross-view LPIPS and RMSE protocol is insufficiently specified and potentially confounded by viewpoint changes, occlusions, and image sharpness. It is unclear whether comparisons use optical-flow or geometry-based correspondence and visibility masks.

The closest feed-forward competitor, Styl3R, is not evaluated. Although the stated reason is unavailable code, this leaves the central claim of superiority in instant 3D stylization supported only against older per-scene methods with materially different operating assumptions.

Geometry preservation is evaluated only through a small reconstruction ablation over three CO3D categories. There is no comparison against the underlying AnySplat/VGGT reconstruction pipeline, no depth or pose evaluation, and no quantitative test showing that arbitrary styles leave geometry unaffected.

The formulation of the central 3D loss is internally unclear: the main text describes aggregating features from different views into a shared voxel grid, whereas Algorithm 3 loops over views and voxelizes and matches statistics separately. As written, the pseudocode does not clearly implement the claimed multi-view 3D fusion.

Reported improvements from the 3D loss are small, with no uncertainty, repeated-run variation, or statistical significance. Scene-level aggregation is nearly tied with image-level matching on several measurements.
The claim of scaling to hundreds of views is not demonstrated: experiments stop at 64 views, training uses at most 24, and the paper reports visible degradation beyond 32 views.

Reproducibility is limited despite the reproducibility statement. Essential details—including loss weights, voxel resolution and bounds, exact architecture configuration, optimizer and schedule, training duration and hardware, view/style sampling, dataset split sizes, rendering protocol, and Gaussian counts—are absent, and code is only promised after acceptance.

The method is substantially built from VGGT/AnySplat geometry, standard cross-attention, and AdaIN-style statistics. The contribution is useful but relatively incremental, and the current evidence does not yet establish a sufficiently strong advance for acceptance at a selective top-tier venue.

strengths: Addresses a useful and timely problem: feed-forward stylization of unposed multi-view inputs without scene-specific optimization.

The separation of geometry prediction from style-conditioned color prediction is intuitive, and the integration of a VGGT/AnySplat-style backbone, global cross-attention, and Gaussian rendering forms a coherent system.
Results show strong short- and long-range consistency on the four evaluated Tanks & Temples scenes, with substantially faster inference than optimization-based methods.
The paper includes relevant architectural and loss ablations, scaling measurements, extensive qualitative results, and candid failure-case analysis.
weaknesses: The central voxel-style-loss claim is weakly supported. Relative to the scene-level loss, improvements in Table 2 are tiny or inconsistent: short-range LPIPS ties, ArtScore changes from 9.12 to 9.15, and long-range RMSE is no better than the image-level baseline. No uncertainty estimates or repeated trials are reported.

The proposed loss matches only global channel-wise mean and variance after voxel fusion. These statistics discard spatial organization and do not directly penalize disagreement between observations of the same 3D location, so the claimed explicit enforcement of 3D or cross-view consistency is stronger than the formulation establishes.

The evaluation is narrow and underspecified. State-of-the-art quantitative comparisons cover only four scenes; sample counts and style-scene pairing protocols are absent; consistency-metric computation, correspondences, visibility handling, and masking are not adequately described; and there is no human perceptual study.

Geometry preservation is a central claim, yet the promised style-free reconstruction evaluation is largely missing. Table 1 evaluates only three CO3D categories as an architectural ablation, with no comparison to reconstruction baselines or comprehensive novel-view geometry metrics.

Comparison fairness is difficult to assess: methods operate at different resolutions, failed StylizedGS cases are selectively excluded and then the method is omitted from primary tables, and optimization-based training time is compared against feed-forward inference. Supplementary quality metrics also generally favor G-Style over Stylos.

The efficiency reporting is internally unclear: Table 4 reports 0.05 s, whereas the scaling study reports roughly 0.3 s even for 1–2 views and excludes rendering cost. The claimed scaling to hundreds of views is not demonstrated, while quality already degrades beyond 32 views.

Novelty is moderate because most components derive from VGGT, AnySplat, standard cross-attention, and AdaIN-style moment matching. Reproducibility is also incomplete: code is only promised, and model size, training hardware, number of GPUs, exact data/style splits, and several implementation details are missing.

strengths: Addresses a relevant problem: fast, pose-free 3D stylization from one to many uncalibrated views.
The separation of geometry prediction from style-conditioned color prediction is intuitive and practically motivated.
The feed-forward pipeline is substantially faster than per-scene optimization methods and is evaluated on unseen scenes, categories, and styles.
Includes several recent baselines, qualitative examples, efficiency measurements, ablations, and candid failure cases.
weaknesses: The main novelty is limited: the method largely combines pretrained VGGT/AnySplat-style reconstruction, standard content-style cross-attention, and AdaIN statistics computed after voxel aggregation. The technical advance beyond these components is modest.

The evidence for the central voxel-level loss is weak. In Table 2, it gives nearly identical results to the scene-level loss, improves ArtScore only from 9.12 to 9.15, and does not consistently improve RMSE. Results use only 15 randomly selected scenes and provide no uncertainty or significance analysis.

The cross-attention ablation measures reconstruction after Stage 1, when a content frame acts as the style reference; it does not establish which coupling strategy produces better artistic stylization. Important baselines such as the pretrained feed-forward reconstruction model with a simpler style-conditioning head are absent.

The evaluation can reward under-stylized or over-smoothed outputs: low cross-view LPIPS/RMSE does not by itself demonstrate faithful style transfer. There is no user study, temporal/video evaluation, or correspondence-aware analysis showing that textures remain attached to 3D surfaces.

Baseline handling is questionable. StylizedGS failure cases are excluded from its reported metrics, while the exclusion criteria and failure frequency are not specified. Styl3R is missing results on one scene, and differences in input resolution and optimization regime further complicate comparisons.

The broader supplementary metrics substantially weaken the quality claim: Stylos is frequently worse than G-Style in FID, LPIPS, grayscale LPIPS, and color-matching loss. The paper mainly demonstrates a speed-quality trade-off rather than clear state-of-the-art stylization quality.

Reproducibility is insufficient. Voxel fusion, occupied/empty-voxel handling, coordinate normalization, visibility and occlusion treatment, confidence computation, style-data splits, sample counts, and evaluation correspondence construction are underspecified. The code link is blank and release is promised only after acceptance.

Reported timing appears inconsistent: Table 4 gives 0.05 s, whereas the appendix reports roughly 0.3 s even for 1–2 views and 0.75 s for 16 views. What computation is included in each number is unclear.

Claims of scaling to hundreds of views are overstated: training uses at most about 20–24 views, quality degrades beyond 32, only up to 64 views is quantitatively profiled, and global self-attention has unfavorable scaling.
The paper does not adequately discuss artist attribution, licensing, memorization, or potential misuse associated with training on and imitating artwork datasets.

strengths: Stylos addresses an important practical gap: feed-forward 3D stylization from unposed inputs, avoiding per-scene optimization while supporting varying numbers of views.

The separation of geometry prediction from style-conditioned color prediction is intuitive and technically well motivated. Global content-style cross-attention and voxel-space feature aggregation form a coherent design.

The paper compares against a broad set of relevant Gaussian-splatting and feed-forward baselines. Stylos obtains the best reported short- and long-range consistency across four Tanks & Temples scenes while being substantially faster than optimization-based methods.

The visual results are generally compelling, with good preservation of scene structure and coherent style propagation. Ablations compare attention topologies and image-, scene-, and voxel-level style objectives, and the appendix includes useful scaling results and candid failure examples.

Testing on held-out CO3D categories, unseen Tanks & Temples scenes, and 50 unseen styles provides meaningful evidence of generalization. Style interpolation and strength control are useful additional capabilities.
weaknesses: The evidence specifically supporting the proposed 3D style loss is modest. Relative to the scene-level loss, improvements in Table 2 are very small or absent—for example, short-range LPIPS is unchanged at 0.047 and ArtScore improves only from 9.12 to 9.15. No uncertainty estimates or repeated-run analysis establish that these differences are significant.

The voxel loss matches only global channel-wise means and standard deviations. Because these statistics discard spatial correspondence, the claim that the loss directly enforces 3D coherence is stronger than the formulation demonstrates. Comparisons to correspondence-aware, reprojection-based, or point/voxel-consistency objectives would better validate this claim.

The main cross-scene quantitative evaluation covers only four Tanks & Temples scenes, and no human preference study is reported. Artistic quality is inherently subjective, while the supplemental metrics often favor G-Style over Stylos; therefore, the broad quality claims are not fully established.

Some comparisons need clearer fairness and protocol reporting. Optimization-based methods operate at full resolution, the feed-forward methods use different preset resolutions, failed StylizedGS cases are selectively excluded, and Styl3R lacks results for one scene. Sample counts, aggregation over the 50 styles, uncertainty, and the exact consistency computation are insufficiently specified.

The reported timing is internally unclear: Table 4 gives 0.05 seconds for Stylos, whereas the scaling study reports roughly 0.3 seconds even for one or two views and 0.75 seconds for 16 views. The view count and included pipeline components must be stated consistently.

Claims of scaling to hundreds of views are not experimentally substantiated: results extend only to 64 views, quality already degrades beyond 32, and training uses at most 20–24 views. Reproducibility is also incomplete because code and weights are only promised upon acceptance, and several details such as hardware/training resources, dataset splits, style-training set construction, and complete loss definitions remain underspecified.

Much of the system builds directly on VGGT and AnySplat, while the new components are relatively simple adaptations. The paper is competitive primarily as a strong system contribution, but the novelty and causal contribution of each component could be established more convincingly.
